      Progress + Drawings Backup

      Safari and the iPad Home Screen app keep separate storage. Use a backup file to move progress, favorites, and saved art between them. Automatic cloud sync is not included.

      Tip: Save the backup in iCloud Drive using Files, open the Home Screen app, and restore that same file there. Export again before switching back.

      How we teach: draw from life, not like a drafting machine

      1. Find the gesture. 2. Place loose mass bubbles and connecting lines. 3. Enclose an organic outer silhouette. 4. Correct proportions and gently erase the scaffolding. 5. Layer meaningful features. 6. Plan and build values, texture, edges and repeated refinements.

      Teaching references: Kimon Nicolaïdes, The Natural Way to Draw (gesture and contour); Andrew Loomis, Figure Drawing for All It's Worth (basic masses and figure construction); Juliette Aristides, Lessons in Classical Drawing (observational block-in and values); James Gurney, Imaginative Realism (believable fantasy from observation, lighting and reference).

      The current 12-stage writing covers all 154 lessons. Hand-drawn stage illustrations are being revised lesson by lesson; Baby Dragon is the first 12-frame revision. Other stage images remain inherited studies and may repeat until replaced. These are teaching principles synthesized into new lesson text, not copied illustrations.
